FINERACT-2338.summary: Allow backdated interest rate change on Progressive loans
FINERACT-2338.description:
h3. Goal

For Progressive loans we should allow backdated interest rate changes
h3. Requirement Details
 # Interest rate can be modified from backdate any date from first disbursement date

 # Interest will be effected from the applied date itself.

 # Backdate can be done on already paid Installments as well

 # Repayment schedule will be recalculated with New EMI and Interest from the Interest applied schedule date

 ## Backdated PAID Installments and Unpaid/Partial Paid Installment EMI would be changed as per the new calculated EMI

 # Installments paid Interest amount will be reverse replayed as per the new Interest rate from the applied date

 ## Transactions will be reversed replayed if there is any change is allocations

 ## Accrual adjustments will done during reverse replay (during the COB process)

 # No of Installments will remain the same, only EMI and Interest would get affected

 # Backdated Interest modification allowed on the loan that is charged off
-If the repayment that was made before the charge-off is reversed and replayed due to backdated Interest modification,then the accounting entry of the reversed transaction and replayed transaction should follow *standard accounting rules and not charge-off accounting rules*

 # Backdated interest modification allowed on the loan that is overpaid, and CBR is complete.
-Fineract, any action that triggers the recalculation (ex: reversal of backdate transaction) on the CBR loan will result in treating CBR as a credit transaction during reverse-replay. Same logic to be applied if the backdated interest modification is allowed on CBR loan accounts

 # Asset transfer (externalization)

 ** If the repayment that was made before the asset owner change got reversed and replayed due to backdated Interest modification,
Then, the accounting entry for the reversed transaction and replayed transaction include the tag of the current asset owner

 # Since backdated Interest modification is allowed on CBR/overpaid loans, we can keep the modification open on closed loans as well

 ** system will do the chronological reverse-replay when the backdated Interest is changed on closed loans, schedule and transaction will be allocated accordingly

FINERACT-2930.summary: Allow adjusting Payout Refund, Goodwill Credit, Charge Adjustment and Merchant Issued Refund transactions
FINERACT-2930.description:
*Background*

The loan transaction adjust endpoint (POST /loans/\{loanId}/transactions/\{transactionId} with a transactionAmountgreater than 0) replaces an existing transaction with a new one that has a new amount and/or date. The original is reversed and the loan's transactions are replayed. Today this only works for Repayment, Waiver and a few other types.

These types can currently be reversed (amount = 0) but not adjusted:
 
 
 
 
||Transaction type||Current behaviour||
|Payout Refund|Blocked by LoanTransaction.isEditable()|
|Goodwill Credit|Blocked by LoanTransaction.isEditable()|
|Merchant Issued Refund|Blocked by LoanTransaction.isEditable()|
|Charge Adjustment|Not handled: the replacement is built as a plain repayment-like transaction, so the link to the adjusted charge is lost|
 
 
 
To change the amount or date of one of these, users have to reverse it and create a new one by hand. That takes two calls, loses the audit link between the old and new transaction, and doesn't work like the other repayment-like types.

*User story*

As a back-office user, I want to adjust the amount and/or date of a Payout Refund, Goodwill Credit, Charge Adjustment or Merchant Issued Refund transaction, so that I can correct it in one step, just as I can with a Repayment.

*Scope*
 # *Payout Refund:* allow adjustment only if the loan product does *not* have automatic Interest Refund enabled for PAYOUT_REFUND (it isn't in supportedInterestRefundTypes).

 # *Merchant Issued Refund:* allow adjustment only if the loan product does *not* have automatic Interest Refund enabled for MERCHANT_ISSUED_REFUND.

 # *Goodwill Credit:* always allow adjustment.

 # *Charge Adjustment:* allow adjustment, keeping the link to the original loan charge.

*Acceptance criteria*

_General (all four types)_
 * Adjusting with transactionAmount > 0 reverses the original transaction and creates a new transaction *of the same type* with the new amount/date. Payment details, external ID and note are handled the same way as for a Repayment adjustment.

 * Reversing (amount = 0) keeps working as it does today.

 * The loan is replayed from the earlier of the original and new transaction dates. The schedule, balances, allocations, accruals and loan status (e.g. closed ↔ active, overpaid) are recalculated correctly.

 * Journal entries are reversed for the original transaction and posted for the new one, using the correct accounts for that transaction type.

 * LoanAdjustTransactionBusinessEvent is raised with both the original and the new transaction detail.

 * Existing checks still apply: account transfer, written-off loan, foreclosed loan, inactive client/group, holiday or non-working day, and transactions that have a chargeback linked to them.

 * LoanTransaction.isEditable() and the allowed-types error message in LoanAdjustmentServiceImpl.adjustExistingTransaction are updated to match.

_Payout Refund / Merchant Issued Refund_
 * If the product has automatic Interest Refund enabled for that type, adjustment is still rejected with a clear error, e.g. error.msg.loan.transaction.adjust.not.allowed.when.interest.refund.enabled. Reversal behaviour doesn't change.

 * If it isn't enabled, adjustment succeeds as described above, and no Interest Refund transaction is created.

_Charge Adjustment_
 * The new transaction stays linked to the same loan charge (LoanChargePaidBy / charge relation).

 * The new amount can't be more than the amount still available for adjustment on that charge, counting the reversed original as available again. Going over it is rejected with the existing "higher than the available charge amount for adjustment" validation.

 * The charge's paid/outstanding amounts and the charge adjustment accounting (income/fee) are recalculated correctly.

_Goodwill Credit_
 * The adjusted Goodwill Credit keeps its own allocation rules and accounting (e.g. the goodwill credit expense account), not the Repayment ones.
*Out of scope*
 * Adjusting Payout Refund or Merchant Issued Refund when automatic Interest Refund is enabled. This needs the linked Interest Refund to be recalculated and belongs in a follow-up.

 * Adjusting Chargeback or Interest Refund transactions.

FINERACT-2934.summary: Merge the two force-withdrawal global configurations into a single one
FINERACT-2934.description:
h2. Background
FINERACT-2471 introduced force withdrawals on savings accounts, controlled by two global configurations (migration {{0217_force_withdrawal_configs.xml}}, released in 1.15.0):

* {{allow-force-withdrawal-on-savings-account}}
* {{force-withdrawal-on-savings-account-limit}}

h2. Observation
The two configurations are redundant. In the code, only one attribute of each is ever read:

* {{ConfigurationDomainServiceJpa#isForceWithdrawalOnSavingsAccountEnabled()}} reads {{isEnabled()}} of {{allow-force-withdrawal-on-savings-account}}.
* {{ConfigurationDomainServiceJpa#retrieveForceWithdrawalOnSavingsAccountLimit()}} reads {{getValue()}} of {{force-withdrawal-on-savings-account-limit}}.

The value of the first one and the enabled flag of the second one are never used. Both are inserted with value=0 and enabled=false, so an administrator has to set two separate rows (and the "enabled" flag of the limit row, although it has no effect, is easy to misread as meaningful).

h2. Proposal
Keep a single configuration, {{allow-force-withdrawal-on-savings-account}}:

* {{enabled}}: whether force withdrawals are allowed (unchanged).
* {{value}}: the maximum negative balance allowed (same meaning and unit as the current limit).

and remove {{force-withdrawal-on-savings-account-limit}}.

Migration (Liquibase, portable across PostgreSQL and MariaDB):

* copy the value of the limit configuration into {{allow-force-withdrawal-on-savings-account}};
* delete the limit configuration row.

For installations that already configured both rows, the effective behaviour does not change.

h2. Code impact (as far as I can see)
* {{GlobalConfigurationConstants}}: remove {{FORCE_WITHDRAWAL_ON_SAVINGS_ACCOUNT_LIMIT}}.
* {{ConfigurationDomainService}} / {{ConfigurationDomainServiceJpa}}: remove {{retrieveForceWithdrawalOnSavingsAccountLimit()}} and read the value of the remaining configuration.
* {{SavingsAccount#isForceWithdrawalAllowed}}: read the limit from the remaining configuration.
* Integration tests and test helpers that list or set the two configurations.

h2. Open questions
# Since the feature shipped in 1.15.0, should the old configuration be removed outright in 1.16.0, or deprecated for one release first?
# What should enabled=true with value=0 mean? Today, with a limit of 0, no negative balance is allowed.
# Should the value be validated as non-negative?
# Does anyone depend on the current configuration names?

h2. Possible follow-up (out of scope for this change)
It would be useful to allow force withdrawals without any limit. I would keep that separate, because the merge above can preserve the current behaviour exactly, while an unlimited overdraft is a different risk decision. If it is wanted, the way to represent "no limit" needs care:

* value=0 is not an option: it means "no negative balance" today and is the default of both rows, so existing installations that enabled the feature without setting a limit would silently become unlimited.
* A negative sentinel such as {{-1}} is not safe either: the current code accepts negative values as valid limits (a negative value is used as is, a positive one is negated), so {{-1}} already means a limit of 1.
* null (the column is nullable) would make "unset" mean "unlimited", which is an unsafe default, and the current code would fail with a NullPointerException.

Whatever the representation, it should be an explicit setting that is never reached by default or by the migration.

Related: FINERACT-2471 (introduced the feature), FINERACT-2797 and FINERACT-2929 (force-withdrawal validation fixes).
